positions.decision: Move away from the enemy King by capturing; straight promotion is legally capturable by the King.

The solver starts in check; capture-promotion both removes the checking rook and meets the material objective. Opposing King is on rank 1 with the captured rook; capture-promotion gives check. This is a composed final-step exercise, not an asserted forced exchange history.
Straight promotion into a King-controlled square is safe because the friendly King protects it; no capture or preparation.
The promoting pawn must vacate the supporting Bishop ray, then occupy the protected capture square next to the enemy King.
Two enemy pieces are available on the last rank; one capture square is King-controlled and the other is safe.
An attractive capture is unsafe; advance without capturing instead. Contrasts with the earlier necessary capture.

A piece blocks the forward square; the pawn cannot capture forward and must use the diagonal capture route. Opposing King is on rank 1 with the captured rook; capture-promotion gives check. This is a composed final-step exercise, not an asserted forced exchange history.
The pawn cannot advance because it shields its King from the Bishop; capturing the pinner on the last rank is legal.
Choose between two promoting pawns: one destination is attacked by the King. The other pawn is protected so the chosen promotion sacrifices nothing.

Choose straight Queen promotion with check over a capture-promotion without check. After fxg1=Q, a8=Q reduces the material gain to three pawn units; f1=Q+ prevents that reply. Rook promotion also allows counter-promotion.
Capture-promotion uncovers a second checking line, so the rook cannot recapture. The friendly King protects the promotion square against King capture.
A different piece is pinned before promotion. The pin prevents recapture by the Bishop; this differs from capturing the pinner with a pinned pawn or uncovering support for the new piece.
